label: myadhd.my
caption:
One "seen" with no reply, and the whole day is gone.

That sting is real, and for a lot of ADHD brains it is louder. Swipe for why a small no hurts this much, and three ways through it.

If this sounded like your brain, come sit with people who get it. Our group is in my bio 👇

Save this for the next time a text goes quiet.

#adhd #adhdmalaysia #myadhd #adhdadult #rejectionsensitivity

slides.title:
Why does a small
[[no]] hurt
this much?
slides.sub: You are not too sensitive. The sting is real.

slides.title:
The sting is
[[bigger]] than
the moment
slides.body: A short reply, a missed invite, a flat "ok". Others shrug it off in a minute. You carry it all afternoon, and it feels like proof of something.

slides.title:
Your brain
[[fills the gap]]
with the worst
slides.body: No reply means busy, or asleep, or driving. But silence leaves a gap, and you fill it with the harshest story you know. Usually it is about you.

slides.title:
Notes on the
work feel like
[[notes on you]]
slides.body: "Can you fix this part?" becomes "I am bad at this". The feedback was about one paragraph. The hurt was about everything.

slides.title:
So you please,
[[pull back]], or
never ask
slides.body: Say yes to everything. Quit before you can be turned down. Never ask at all. They look like different habits. They are the same shield.

slides.title:
Name it before
you [[believe it]]
slides.body: "This is the sting, not the facts." Saying it plainly puts a little space between the feeling and the story it is telling you.

slides.title:
Wait an [[hour]]
before you
reply
slides.body: The urge to explain, apologise or cut them off is strongest in the first hour. Write the message if you must. Send it tomorrow, if it still makes sense.

slides.title:
Ask, instead
of [[guessing]]
slides.body: "Hey, was that ok?" is a small question. It costs far less than a night of rereading their last message for hidden meaning.

slides.title:
Save this for the
next time a text
[[goes quiet]]
slides.body: The feeling is loud, but it is not a verdict on you. Dump the spiral into my.adhd and get one thing back to do instead.
